title: The final Amen (CCC 2855–2865)
hook: the Catechism ends where prayer ends: Amen

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last four petitions: bread, forgiveness, temptation, deliverance. Your line was give, forgive, lead, deliver. Did you catch yourself saying us instead of me? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-one.

A thick book, set on a table. It holds the creed line by line, the sacraments one by one, the commandments, and then a long walk through prayer. And when you turn to its very last paragraph, the thing it's talking about is one small word. Not a doctrine. Not a rule. A word said at the end of prayers, often without stopping to think about it. The Catechism of the Catholic Church closes on Amen. We've been reading it part by part since the start of this year, and today we reach that same last word. Today: the final Amen.
screen: `A THICK BOOK.` → `ITS LAST PARAGRAPH.` → `ONE SMALL WORD.`

segments.voice: First, what comes just before it. In the Douay-Rheims, Matthew's Our Father ends simply: "But deliver us from evil. Amen." Christians who use the King James wording go straight on: "For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever." At Mass, Catholics say words of praise much like these too, after a short prayer by the priest. The Catechism says this praise gathers up the first three petitions, the name, the kingdom, the will, and hands them back to God. Then the Amen. The Catechism quotes Cyril of Jerusalem, teaching new Christians: after the prayer is over, you say Amen, which means so be it, and so you put your seal on everything the prayer contains. A signature at the bottom of a letter. In its final paragraph, the Catechism goes one step further: the last Amen is our own yes to all seven petitions. Days ago we met Mary's yes at the angel's word. Here every person who prays gets to say one like it. And in the book of Revelation, Christ himself is given the name: "These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness." So the word that ends the prayer is also, for Catholics, a name for the one the prayer goes through. Now look back. The Catechism has four parts, and we've walked them all this year: what the Church believes, how it celebrates, how it lives, and how it prays. It ends with a word a small child can say.
screen: `THINE IS THE KINGDOM.` · `AMEN: SO BE IT, A SEAL.` · `OUR YES TO EVERY PETITION.` · `FOUR PARTS, ONE LAST WORD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: close the part with Amen. Settle, and breathe. If you pray, choose one line of the Our Father you most want to mean today. Say it, then answer it with one deliberate Amen, like a signature. If there's time, take another line. If you don't pray, think back over the months of this part: one belief, one sacrament, one way of living, one prayer that stayed with you. Hold them together, and let them rest. The bell holds the time.
The final Amen. The last word of the Our Father, and the subject of the Catechism's last paragraph: so be it, our yes to everything the prayer asks. Today's words.

Your line: amen. Today, the next time you say yes to something, a request, a plan, a person, say it the way Cyril describes Amen: as a signature you mean. Tomorrow a new part begins, with a boy locked in a tower. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-one.

screen: `DAY 1151 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE BOY IN THE TOWER.`

howItsDone: Catholics end their prayers with Amen and answer Amen many times during Mass, including when receiving Communion; at Mass, the Our Father is followed by a short prayer of the priest and then the people's words of praise to God's kingdom, power and glory.

pairs: a name for Christ in Revelation

myth: the Douay-Rheims Our Father in Matthew includes for thine is the kingdom
it ends "But deliver us from evil. Amen." the King James wording adds the words of praise.
Cyril of Jerusalem taught that saying Amen seals what the prayer contains
the Catechism quotes him: Amen means so be it.
the Catechism ends with a long list of rules
its last paragraph is about the final Amen: our yes to every petition.

fork.setup: you're a new Christian, hearing Cyril of Jerusalem explain the Our Father. you reach the last word. what does he tell you it does?
options: it simply means the prayer is over.
it means so be it, sealing what was prayed.
it's a word only the priest may say.
fork.reveal: Cyril, quoted in the Catechism: after the prayer you say Amen, which means so be it, and so you seal what God has taught you to ask.

original.note: Hebrew: amen — a word from the Hebrew scriptures; Cyril explains it as "so be it."

trapdoor: what you thought: amen is how you signal the prayer is finished.
what it means: amen means so be it: a signature on everything the prayer asked, our own yes to each petition.
what a scholar hears: the Catechism quotes Cyril of Jerusalem's teaching to new Christians, and its final paragraph calls the last Amen our fiat to the seven petitions.
